tasks.do: BEFORE and AFTER in one command. `node build/tools/review/evidence.mjs --before --brief <spec.json>` plays only the rows the brief's tasks name (their evidence.json probes), at the brief's sizes (default 1366x768 and 915x412), as crops and short filmstrips (strip:<sel>:<n>x<ms> for anything that moves; 250 and 500 ms by default), and stores them as that brief's 'before'. `--after --brief <spec.json>` does the same after the build. Reuse --run, the verdict log and redGreen; add no second capture path. A row with no probe refuses the brief (as today). New features (rows that describe something not yet built) need no red: their before panel is simply 'not there yet'.
tasks.accept: a worked example on 2-3 real rows (e.g. SH-19 the finger, a glow row, a help-box row): the before and after folders exist, named by brief and row; the unit tests cover the brief-to-rows step

tasks.do: The judge's batch is made by the script: `--judge --brief <spec>` writes batches where each row's sheet shows BEFORE beside AFTER (same moment, same size, same crop), panels labelled, its words on top. The judge passes a row only when before shows the problem (or 'not there yet' for a new feature) AND after shows it fixed; a before that does not show the problem is EVIDENCE (a probe fault), never PASS. Update .claude/agents/judge.md for this, keeping it short. `--before --check` lets the orchestrator send just the before sheets to the judge at launch, to prove the probes see the problem before the builder starts.
tasks.accept: a batch file and its sheets for the worked example; the judge.md diff

tasks.do: The side-by-side sheet per shared element (kitsheet). data/kit-elements.json lists each element (face circle, word card, order card, order pop-up, bubble, buttons, finger, help box, glow, '?' pop-up, end screen, to-record text) with its selector(s) and where it shows (flow, moment) on every LIVE page (index, first, day, cook, clinic, lab; the parked games are out). `node build/tools/review/kitsheet.mjs --elem <name> [--before|--after]` crops that element from every page at 1366x768 and 915x412 into one sheet (game name under each crop), plus a 2-4 frame strip for moving ones (glow, finger, hop). The judge passes the element on that sheet: same look in every game. An element not reachable on a page is listed as such on the sheet, never silently dropped.
tasks.accept: kitsheets for the finger, the glow and the order card from today's game, at both sizes; the list of any page/moment no driver reaches yet
